title: Scan4D Derived Surfaces JSON Schema
description: Per-scan walkable surfaces recovered from the classified mesh, written to `derived_surfaces.json` in the scan directory and mirrored to `raw_data/`. These are the surfaces RoomPlan did not model — steps, landings, mezzanines, shallow ramps — since RoomPlan models one floor per room. Generated at Process time by the ghost-proxy build from the same inputs as `mesh_proxy.obj` (`mesh.obj` + `face_classes.bin`), so it is co-framed with the mesh and the proxy and is regenerated rather than transformed whenever they are; its staleness rides the ghost-proxy version header. This is an on-device artifact and is NOT included in any export archive. Absent when a scan produced no derived surfaces, which is the normal case for a flat single-level room.

version.description: Schema version. Currently 1. Readers reject any version other than the current one rather than attempting a partial decode; the file regenerates on the next Process.

surfaces.description: Derived walkable planes; levels are emitted before ramps. Never empty when the file exists — a rebuild that finds nothing deletes the file rather than leaving a stale answer.

surface.description: An oriented plane for one derived walkable surface. Unlike a roomplan.json surface it carries no `id` and no `confidence`, and the file has no `source` field.

category.description: 'level' = a walkable horizontal surface at a distinct height; 'ramp' = a coherently sloped walkable plane. Deliberately never 'floor': the plane-registration decoder accepts only 'wall' and 'floor', so a decoder pointed at this file drops these surfaces rather than feeding them silently into a coordinate solve. A ramp is not interchangeable with a level there — the fit's plane matcher admits pairs up to 25 degrees apart, so a shallow ramp would correspond to a flat floor and pull the vertical solution with it. Consumers must opt in per category.

dimensions.description: Extent in the surface's own plane, in meters.

transform.description: 4x4 transform placing the surface in the scan's world space (column-major, 16 floats): col0 = xAxis, col1 = yAxis, col2 = plane normal, col3 = center. Same convention as roomplan.json.

dimensions.description: Planar extent in meters. This is the bounding rectangle of the mesh faces that contributed to the surface, not the room footprint.

width.description: Extent along the transform's first column (meters).

height.description: Extent along the transform's second column (meters).

depth.description: Always 0 — a derived surface is a plane, not a volume. Present only so the shape matches roomplan.json's dimensions for renderers that consume both.

flatMatrix4x4.description: A 4x4 matrix flattened to 16 floats in column-major order: [c0r0, c0r1, c0r2, c0r3, c1r0, c1r1, c1r2, c1r3, c2r0, c2r1, c2r2, c2r3, c3r0, c3r1, c3r2, c3r3]. Matches the convention used by roomplan.json, stitching.json and transforms.json.
